notes.content: This agreement primarily displays only the lower-division courses required in the major, and a few featured upper-division courses. Although completion of the coursework below is not necessarily mandatory prior to admission, students are strongly advised to complete as much lower division course preparation as possible prior to transfer. This agreement does not contain most upper-division (junior-senior) major requirements, course pre-requisites, general education or all-university coursework necessary for completion of this degree. notes.content: A B.A. with a major in linguistics requires 36-46 units completed, depending on which option, the General Education requirement, specific course/skill requirements, and electives and remaining degree requirements totaling at least the 120 units required for a B.A. In each option, students receive a basic grounding in the nature and structure of human language. The option in Interdisciplinary Language Studies supplements the core foundation with extensive study in one or more languages other than English, and can thus prepare students for work in translating and interpreting, among other careers where extensive knowledge of language is required. Advising Notes CR/NC grading is not permitted in the linguistics major. See advisor for list of approved electives. Students who have studied a language in high school or community college, or who by culture and experience have a certain level of proficiency, must consult with an advisor in the language to determine their placement in lower- or upper-division coursework. Students must fulfill the unit requirement by taking language courses in a minimum of two languages. Students must maintain a B average in the languages taken. Literature courses in the language may be used with permission of advisor. Except for LING 120 and LING 121, courses taught in English do not count toward the required courses for Plan A or Plan B. In addition to the major program requirements, every student must also complete the University’s baccalaureate degree requirements such as: American Government and Institutions ( PLSI 2 ) General Education Requirements (43 units) Additional University Graduation Requirements (9 units) Upper-Division Writing Requirement General Education, Additional University Graduation Requirements, and Upper-division Writing courses can be double counted with major requirements. Language IB Courses could fulfill GE Area 3B. See advisor for details. Sufficient Elective Units to Meet Required Total Units (varies); it is recommended that units in this area be utilized to complete a second major or minor. A full description of the University’s graduation requirements can be found in the Baccalaureate Degree Requirements .
notes.contentHtml:
A B.A. with a major in linguistics requires 36-46 units completed, depending on which option, the General Education requirement, specific course/skill requirements, and electives and remaining degree requirements totaling at least the 120 units required for a B.A.


In each option, students receive a basic grounding in the nature and structure of human language. The option in Interdisciplinary Language Studies supplements the core foundation with extensive study in one or more languages other than English, and can thus prepare students for work in translating and interpreting, among other careers where extensive knowledge of language is required.


Advising Notes

CR/NC grading is not permitted in the linguistics major.

  • See advisor for list of approved electives.
  • Students who have studied a language in high school or community college, or who by culture and experience have a certain level of proficiency, must consult with an advisor in the language to determine their placement in lower- or upper-division coursework.
  • Students must fulfill the unit requirement by taking language courses in a minimum of two languages. Students must maintain a B average in the languages taken.
  • Literature courses in the language may be used with permission of advisor. Except for LING 120 and LING 121, courses taught in English do not count toward the required courses for Plan A or Plan B.


In addition to the major program requirements, every student must also complete the University’s baccalaureate degree requirements such as:

  • American Government and Institutions (PLSI 2)
  • General Education Requirements (43 units)
  • Additional University Graduation Requirements (9 units)
  • Upper-Division Writing Requirement
  • General Education, Additional University Graduation Requirements, and Upper-division Writing courses can be double counted with major requirements. Language IB Courses could fulfill GE Area 3B. See advisor for details.
  • Sufficient Elective Units to Meet Required Total Units (varies); it is recommended that units in this area be utilized to complete a second major or minor.

A full description of the University’s graduation requirements can be found in the Baccalaureate Degree Requirements.

notes.content: Additional University Graduation Requirements The Additional University Graduation Requirements are designed to complement the GE requirements. It is the policy of Fresno State, that all students will cultivate and refine their affective, cognitive, and physical faculties through studying great works of the human imagination; be equipped for lifelong understanding and development of themselves as integrated physiological, social, and psychological beings; and be prepared to understand and live in a multicultural and international world through their undergraduate education. This will be accomplished through a total of 9 units from the following areas, each requiring 3 units: Arts/Humanities (A/H) - All students are required to take an Arts/Humanities course to graduate at the bachelor’s degree level. Lifelong-Understanding and Self-Development (L/S) - All students are required to take a lifelong understanding and self-development course to for graduate at the bachelor’s degree level. Multicultural/International (M/I) - All Students are required to take a Multicultural / International course at Fresno State to graduate at the bachelor’s degree level.
notes.contentHtml:
Additional University Graduation Requirements


The Additional University Graduation Requirements are designed to complement the GE requirements. It is the policy of Fresno State, that all students will cultivate and refine their affective, cognitive, and physical faculties through studying great works of the human imagination; be equipped for lifelong understanding and development of themselves as integrated physiological, social, and psychological beings; and be prepared to understand and live in a multicultural and international world through their undergraduate education.

This will be accomplished through a total of 9 units from the following areas, each requiring 3 units:

  1. Arts/Humanities (A/H) - All students are required to take an Arts/Humanities course to graduate at the bachelor’s degree level. 
  2. Lifelong-Understanding and Self-Development (L/S) - All students are required to take a lifelong understanding and self-development course to for graduate at the bachelor’s degree level. 
  3. Multicultural/International (M/I) - All Students are required to take a Multicultural / International course at Fresno State to graduate at the bachelor’s degree level.

notes.content: PLAN A (Section 1) - DEPTH PLAN in One Language (Lower division major requirements section one) Select one language (French, Spanish, German, Japanese, Chinese, or Hmong) If French or Spanish is selected, 9 elective units need to be approved by the advisor. PLAN B (Section 2) - BREADTH PLAN (Lower division major requirements section two) Select a minimum of two languages but not more than three languages (American Sign Language, Arabic, Armenian, Chinese, French, German, Greek, Hebrew, Hmong, Italian, Japanese, Latin, Persian, Portuguese, Sanskrit, Spanish).

PLAN A (Section 1) - DEPTH PLAN in One Language (Lower division major requirements section one) Select one language (French, Spanish, German, Japanese, Chinese, or Hmong) If French or Spanish is selected, 9 elective units need to be approved by the advisor.


PLAN B (Section 2) - BREADTH PLAN (Lower division major requirements section two) Select a minimum of two languages but not more than three languages (American Sign Language, Arabic, Armenian, Chinese, French, German, Greek, Hebrew, Hmong, Italian, Japanese, Latin, Persian, Portuguese, Sanskrit, Spanish).
